lead: Portland plumbing deals with long cold winters, old wood-frame homes and oil heat. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Portland, Maine.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in old homes and boiler and heating issues
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and boilers
why: The West End, Munjoy Hill and Deering have homes from the 1800s and early 1900s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals. Many are multi-unit buildings.
Long, cold winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Many homes use oil or gas boilers, so heating and plumbing problems often overlap.
water: Portland Water District draws from Sebago Lake, one of the few large U.S. sources clean enough to skip filtration. The water is very soft.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Have your boiler serviced before winter.
Know where each unit's shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in the West End, Munjoy Hill, the Old Port, Deering, Back Cove, Libbytown, Stroudwater and every other Portland neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Portland Permitting and Inspections Department, and plumbers must be licensed by the Maine Plumbers' Examining Board.

faq.q: Is this Portland, Maine or Portland, Oregon?
faq.a: This page covers Portland, Maine. For Portland, Oregon, see our Portland, Oregon page. PipeMend serves both.
